instruction: Make me a Spotify playlist called "My Highest Rated Playlist Songs" containing only the highest-rated song from each of my playlists.
notes: Single-app (spotify) task. The user's playlist library is modeled by a representative set of two existing playlists with two songs each; at runtime the library listing (all pages) and each show_playlist response determine the real number of playlists/songs, and the show_song/add pattern is repeated per playlist. Because PDDL has no numeric comparison here, the ground-truth 'highest-rated' relation is a static hidden world fact in :init that the agent only learns by calling show_song on every song of the playlist: add_song_to_playlist requires (rating-known) for the chosen song and for the other song of the same source playlist, so the plan must inspect all songs before adding. show_playlist ids become usable only after show_playlist_library (library-shown); song ids only after show_playlist of their playlist (songs-known). Extra non-API parameters are task records: the created playlist object in create_playlist (bound to the returned playlist_id), the source playlist in show_song/add_song_to_playlist, and the compared song in add_song_to_playlist. supervisor-complete-task takes no API arguments (no answer); its record parameters exist only so its precondition can restate the goal (titled new playlist and the highest-rated song of each user playlist added to it). Only the new playlist and its PlaylistSong rows are changed, matching the evaluation.
